name: Immunodeficiency due to a classical component pathway complement deficiency

criteria.description: Demonstrated low or absent classical complement pathway activity by CH50 assay
Identification of pathogenic variants in classical complement component genes (C1q, C1r, C1s, C2, C4A, C4B)
History of recurrent invasive infections with encapsulated bacteria such as Neisseria meningitidis
Positive family history of complement deficiency or related immunodeficiency
Normal alternative and lectin pathway complement activity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low classical pathway activity, pathogenic genetic variant in classical complement component gene, and history of recurrent invasive bacterial infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other complement pathway deficiencies and secondary causes of complement consumption.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic susceptibility to Neisseria species infections

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe invasive infections with encapsulated bacteria
pathognomonic.notes: Includes Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae infections
searchTerms: severe infections with protective capsule bacteria
infections from bacteria with outer coating

common.notes: Specifically low C2, C4, or C1 components
searchTerms: low complement levels in blood test

common.symptomName: Autoimmune manifestations such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like symptoms
common.notes: May include arthritis, rash, and nephritis

common.symptomName: Chronic fatigue related to recurrent infections
searchTerms: persistent fatigue due to repeated infections

occasional.notes: Inflammatory skin lesions due to immune complex deposition
Joint pain related to autoimmune phenomena

rare.notes: Fulminant autoimmune disease in rare cases

searchTerms: severe allergic reaction to blood transfusion

laboratory: Low or absent CH50 (classical complement pathway) activity
Normal AH50 (alternative pathway) and lectin pathway activity
Reduced serum levels of classical complement components (C1q, C1r, C1s, C2, C4)
Presence of pathogenic mutations in complement component genes
imaging: Imaging may show complications of infections such as meningitis or pneumonia
Renal ultrasound may reveal changes consistent with glomerulonephritis
other: Family history of complement deficiency or recurrent severe infections
Positive response to prophylactic antibiotics or immunizations

distinguishingFeatures: Different genetic mutations affecting alternative pathway components

redFlags: Severe invasive infections with encapsulated bacteria despite vaccination
Early onset autoimmune manifestations resembling lupus
references: Jónsson et al., Classical complement pathway deficiencies and susceptibility to infections, Clinical Immunology, 2020
Orphanet Report on Classical Complement Deficiencies, 2023
Walport MJ. Complement. First of two parts. N Engl J Med. 2001 Apr 5;344(14):1058-66.
